Summarize Brown Heart Assistant..answer: The Brown Heart Assistant (BHAI) is a full‑stack, citation‑grounded health‑education platform that Pranav built from scratch, now serving more than 5,000 users and complemented by a searchable FAQ site [1]. It uses a router‑orchestrated multi‑agent architecture that routes queries to specialized agents for FAQ, the MASALA Study, Instagram, YouTube, and movie‑timestamp content, each operating with source‑grounded prompts, confidence gating, and medical‑safety refusal logic [1]. Its retrieval layer combines BM25, Azure PostgreSQL/pgvector, HNSWlib, and NVIDIA embeddings with reciprocal‑rank‑fusion and Azure OpenAI for chat generation, while a human‑in‑the‑loop tool handles low‑confidence medical queries for doctor‑specialty matching or appointment booking [2]. The production backend includes Azure Blob artifact hydration, checksum validation, signed sessions, admin health checks, environment‑based model configuration, LangSmith tracing, and a suite of 113 passing tests [2]. Reliability is reinforced through query analysis, hybrid retrieval, Neo4j knowledge graphs, multi‑step evidence‑sufficiency audits, and strict confidence‑gating thresholds to prevent hallucinations [3].

citations.title: RAG Reliability & Audits
citations.snippet: Pranav approaches RAG reliability by building self-correcting architectures. In projects like Agentic Graph-RAG (The Brain) and Brown Heart Assistant, he ensures high reliability using query analysis, hybrid retrieval (BM25 + vector matching), Neo4j knowledge graphs, multi-step evidence sufficiency audits, confidence gating thresholds, and medical-safety refusal filters to prevent hallucinations.

How does he approach RAG reliability?.answer: Pranav ensures RAG reliability by designing self‑correcting architectures that continuously audit and refine the retrieval‑generation pipeline. He begins with thorough query analysis and employs hybrid retrieval that combines BM25 keyword matching with dense vector search (FAISS/Pinecone) and a Neo4j knowledge graph to broaden evidence sources [1]. During inference the system runs multi‑step evidence‑sufficiency audits, applies confidence‑gating thresholds, and uses medical‑safety refusal filters to block hallucinations [1]. If a query lacks adequate support, the agent expands the search to the web or Wikipedia via Tavily, verifies the returned snippets, and applies HyDE query‑expansion before producing a final answer [2].

citations.title: Agentic Graph-RAG: The Brain
citations.snippet: Pranav built 'Agentic Graph-RAG: The Brain', a self-correcting LangGraph agent that audits evidence sufficiency, expands searches to web/Wikipedia via Tavily when needed, verifies supporting snippets, and refines failed queries with HyDE query expansion before answering. It uses hybrid retrieval across FAISS/Pinecone dense vectors, BM25, and a 311K-node / 374K-edge Neo4j knowledge graph over 39K chunks, unified with NVIDIA and Cross-Encoder reranking. On 100 judged SQuAD-style examples it improved retrieval hit rate from 82% to 92% and LLM-judged faithfulness from 0.708 to 0.847.
